text:
Ottawa won this one on the scoreboard while Philadelphia won it on the ice. The Flyers piled up 3.4 expected goals to the Senators' 2.27 and out-attempted them 64 to 50, which is why they deserved to win 70 percent of the time if you replay every shot. Nick Cousins gave Ottawa the early lead on a tip-in at 10:14 of the first, a chance worth just 11 percent, and the Senators spent most of the night living off that kind of thing.

The second period was the Flyers' best stretch, and it was lopsided. They generated 1.97 expected goals to Ottawa's 0.68, and Matvei Michkov cashed in on the power play at 7:46 with a backhand that carried an 85 percent chance of scoring. Trevor Zegras and Travis Konecny set it up, and Konecny's line owned the territory with 2.03 expected goals for against 0.44 against. Linus Ullmark was the reason it stayed 1-1. He faced 29 shots worth 3.4 expected goals and allowed one, a gain of 2.4 goals over what an average goalie would have managed.

The winner came on the power play at 13:01 of the third, when Carter Yakemchuk's slap shot, a 6 percent chance, found its way through after Claude Giroux and Shane Pinto fed him. Joseph Woll stopped 24 of 26, close to what the chances demanded, so the loss sits less on him than on a game where Philadelphia couldn't turn volume into goals. The Flyers blocked 20 shots to Ottawa's 11, but the Senators got the two bounces that mattered and Ullmark did the rest.
